questions.question: According to the Indian calendar, Hemanta season falls in which months?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Margashirsa-Pausa.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hemanta season:-**

 
 
• **​It **falls in the months of **Margashirsa-Pausa** according to the Indian calendar.
 
• Hemanta is one of the **six seasons **mentioned in the Indian calendar, which is based on the **position of the sun**
 
• Hemanta season is also known as the** pre-winter season** and is characterized by **cool and dry** weather.
 
• The months of Margashirsa-Pausa fall between **November-December **and **December-January** respectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sravana-Bhadra:-**

 
 
• Itis a combination of two months in the Indian calendar and falls during the monsoon season** (July-August/ August-September).**
 
 
 
• **Chaitra-Vaisakha:-**
 
 
• It is the period between** March-April and April-May** and marks the beginning of the spring season.
 
 
 
• **Jyaistha-Asadha:-**
 
 
• It is the period between **May-June and June-July** and marks the beginning of the summer season.

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest boiling point?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alkynes.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alkynes:-**

 
 
• **​**These have the **highest boiling point **among the given options due to their** strong intermolecular forces of attraction.**
 
• Alkynes have **triple bonds** between carbon atoms, which results in a **linear shape **and** close packing of molecules**, leading to** strong van der Waals forces.**
 
• **Alkanes** have **weaker intermolecular forces **due to their **single bonds** and** branched structures**, resulting in **lower boiling points.**
 
• **Alkenes **have** double bonds**, which create a kink in the molecule and reduce the surface area available for intermolecular interactions, leading to **lower boiling points.**
 
• **Free carbon dioxide** is a gas at room temperature and pressure, and hence, it has the** lowest boiling point** among the given options.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkanes**: 

 
 
• These are hydrocarbons with **single bonds** between carbon atoms, and their **boiling points increase** with** increasing chain length **and **molecular weight.**
 
 
 
• **Alkenes: **
 
 
• **​**These are hydrocarbons with **double bonds** between carbon atoms, and their** boiling points are lower** than those of corresponding alkanes due to their lower intermolecular forces.
 
 
 
• **Free carbon dioxide:** 
 
 
• It is a **gas at room temperature **and pressure and is formed during **respiration, combustion,** and other processes. 
 
 
• It has a boiling point of **-78.5oC** at standard temperature and pressure.

questions.question: Identify the function of lipase in the process of digestion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Breaking down emulsified fats.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lipase** is an **enzyme** that plays a crucial role in the **digestion of fats in the body.**
 
• The **breakdown of fats** is essential for the **absorption and utilization** of essential **fatty acids and fat-soluble vitamins**.
 
• **Lipase breaks down emulsified fats**:
 
 
• The process of digestion starts in the** mouth** where the food is chewed and mixed with** saliva.**
 
• Saliva contains an enzyme called **salivary lipase **that starts breaking down fats.
 
• However, the majority of **fat digestion** happens in the** small intestine** where the emulsified fats are acted upon by **pancreatic lipase.**
 
• This enzyme breaks down the emulsified fats into** fatty acids and glycerol, **which can be absorbed by the body.
 
 
 
• **Lipase works with bile:**
 
 
• Bile is a **digestive fluid** produced by the** liver **and stored in the **gallbladder.**
 
• Bile contains bile salts that help in the **emulsification of fats**, making them easier for** lipase to break down.**
 
• Lipase and bile work together to **digest fats **and ensure their **absorption **in the body.
 
 
 
• **Lipase deficiency can lead to malabsorption:**
 
 
• In some cases, people may have a **deficiency of lipase,** which can result in **malabsorption of fats.**
 
• This can lead to symptoms like **bloating, gas, diarrhea, and weight loss.**
 
• People with conditions like c**ystic fibrosis, pancreatitis, and celiac disease **may have a deficiency of lipase.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Breaking down roughage:** This is the function of enzymes like **cellulase**, which break down the fiber in plant foods.

 
 
• Lipase **does not** play a role in breaking down roughage.
 
 
 
• **Secreting intestinal fluids:** This is the function of the **intestinal glands**, which secrete fluids that help in the digestion and absorption of nutrients.
 
 
• Lipase is **not** involved in this process.
 
 
 
• **Digesting proteins**: This is the function of enzymes like** pepsin and trypsin**, which break down proteins into amino acids.
 
 
• Lipase does **not** play a role in digesting proteins.
 
 
 
• Hence, the** correct **option is 2) Breaking down emulsified fats.

questions.question: The maximum distance covered in a marathon is __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42.195 km.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The maximum distance covered in a marathon is 42.195 km.
 
• This is the **standard distance** for a marathon according to the** International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF).**
 
• The distance was set in **1921** for the **Olympic Games **held in **London** and has since become the standard distance for marathons worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A** marathon** is a **long-distance race** with a distance of 42.195 kilometers or **26.2 miles.**
 
• The race is named after the **Greek soldier Pheidippides **who ran from the** city of Marathon to Athens** to deliver the news of victory against the **Persians **in **490 BCE.**
 
• 40 km is the distance for some** ultramarathons**, but not for a standard marathon.
 
• 42.5 km is the distance for the **Comrades Marathon** held in** South Africa**, which is an ultramarathon.
 
• 41.5 km is the distance for the** Jungfrau Marathon** held in **Switzerland**, which is a mountain marathon.

questions.question: Who was the president of the second session of the Indian National Congress?

• Naoroji was a prominent economist and is known for his theories on the economic exploitation of India by the British colonial administration.
 
• He highlighted the concept of the "Drain of Wealth," which referred to the economic resources being drained from India to Britain due to colonial policies.
 
• One of Naoroji's most famous works is the book titled "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India," published in 1901.

• **Pherozeshah Mehta:-**
 
 
• He​ was a** lawyer, social reformer, and political leader** who played a prominent role in the Indian National Congress and the Indian independence movement.
 
 
 
• **George Yule:-**
 
 
• **​**He was a **British businessman **who served as the president of the Indian National Congress in 1888**.**

questions.question:
Which of the following is a negative effect of Green Revolution in India?

(i) Depletion of groundwater table

(ii) Deterioration in the quality of soil

(iii) Increased input cost
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i), (ii) and (iii).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Green Revolution:-**

 
 
• It​ was a significant development in **India's agricultural sector **that aimed to increase **agricultural productivity** and **reduce food insecurity.**
 
• **However, it also had some negative effects.**
 
 
 
• **Depletion of groundwater table:-**
 
 
• The Green Revolution promoted the use of** high-yielding crop varieties,** which required **more water for irrigation.**
 
• As a result, farmers started **extracting groundwater **at an** unsustainable rate,** leading to a decline in the groundwater table.
 
• This, in turn, led to **water scarcity **and affected the livelihoods of farmers who depended on groundwater for irrigation.
 
 
 
• **Deterioration in the quality of soil:-**
 
 
• The use of** chemical fertilizers and pesticides** was a key feature of the Green Revolution.
 
• Over time, this led to **soil degradation, loss of soil fertility,** and **reduced crop yields.**
 
• **Soil erosion, salinization, and acidification **were some of the other negative impacts on soil quality.
 
 
 
• **Increased input cost:-**
 
 
• The adoption of **new technologies and practices** under the Green Revolution required farmers to invest in expensive inputs like** seeds, fertilizers, and machinery.**
 
• This increased the** cost of cultivation**, making it difficult for **small and marginal farmers** to afford these inputs.
 
• As a result, they had to** borrow money **from moneylenders at** high-interest rates,** leading to a **cycle of debt and poverty.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:** It refers to the period of **rapid agricultural development** in the **1960s and 1970s, **which aimed to **increase food production** through the use of **high-yielding crop varieties, chemical fertilizers, and pesticides.**
 
• **Positive Effects:** The Green Revolution led to a significant **increase in food production, reduced food prices, and improved food security** in India.
 
 
• It also created new** job opportunities** and** increased rural income.**
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Agriculture: **It refers to an agricultural system that is** environmentally friendly, socially just, and economically viable.** 
 
 
• It promotes the use of **organic farming practices, crop diversification**, and **conservation of natural resources.**

questions.question:
Select the option that is true regarding the following two statements labelled Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

(A): An object slips less on a rough surface than a smooth surface.

(R): When a surface is rough, frictional force increases.

options.text: Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are the true but Reason (R) is not a correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is true.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are the true and Reason (R) is a correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are the true and Reason (R) is a correct explanation of Assertion (A).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A) **is **true** because a **rough surface** provides more contact points between the **object and the surface**, increasing the** frictional force** and **reducing slipping.**
 
• **Reason (R)** is also **true** because** frictional force increases** with **roughness **as the **irregularities** in the surface create more resistance.
 
• Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are** related and true,** and Reason (R) provides a **correct explanation **for Assertion (A).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frictional force:-**

 
 
• It is a force that **opposes motion** between two surfaces** in contac**t.
 
• It is dependent on the** nature of the surfaces** in contact, the **normal force**, and the **coefficient of friction.**

questions.question: On 1 February 2021, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman informed that _________ and _________ will be merged under the umbrella of Mission POSHAN 2.0.

options.text: Supplementary Health Programme; National health Mission
Supplementary Nutrition Programme; National Health Mission
Supplementary Nutrition Programme; National Nutrition Mission
Supplementary Health Programme; National Nutrition Mission

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Supplementary Nutrition Programme; National Nutrition Mission.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The** Supplementary Nutrition Programme (SNP):-**

 
 
• It​ is a **government initiative **aimed at improving the **nutritional status **of** pregnant and lactating mothers, infants, and children **under the age of** 6 years.**
 
• The program provides** free food **to the beneficiaries and aims to** reduce malnutrition and stunting.**
 
 
 
• **National Nutrition Mission** (NNM):-
 
 
• It is a flagship program of the government launched in **2018** with the aim of **reducing malnutrition** among children and women.
 
• The program provides a comprehensive approach to address** malnutrition** through various interventions such as the promotion of** breastfeeding, dietary diversification, **and **the use of fortified foods.**
 
 
 
• **Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced the merger of two programs under the umbrella of Mission POSHAN 2.0. The two programs are the Supplementary Nutrition Programme and the National Nutrition Mission.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mission POSHAN 2.0:-**

 
 
• **It is a continuation and expansion of the Government of India's efforts to address malnutrition and improve the nutritional status of women, children, and adolescents. **
 
• It focuses on ensuring a more comprehensive and multi-sectoral approach to combat malnutrition. Some key points about Mission POSHAN 2.0:
 
• It utilizes technology for real-time monitoring, data collection, and assessment of nutritional interventions, aiding in better planning and implementation.
 
• The mission focuses on behavior change communication, aiming to promote better nutritional practices and habits at the community level.
 
• Adequate budget allocation is crucial for the successful implementation of the mission's strategies and interventions.
